What is the ratio of number of seats that remained vacant in all the Non-AC classes on Wednesday and Thursday taken together to number of seats remained vacant in AC classes on Monday, Tuesday and Friday
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The number of seat remained vacant in 2nd class Non-AC on Wednesday = (900 – 830) = 70

The number of seat remained vacant in 2nd class Non-AC on Thursday = (900 – 790) = 110

The number of seat remained vacant in 1st class Non-AC on Wednesday = (500 – 390) = 110

The number of seat remained vacant in 1st class Non-AC on Thursday = (500 – 480) = 20

Total number of vacant seat in all the Non-AC classes on Wednesday and Thursday = (70 + 110 + 110 + 20)

⇒ 310

The number of seat remained vacant in AC III tier on Monday = (500 – 480) = 20

The number of seat remained vacant in AC III tier on Tuesday = (500 – 450) = 50

The number of seat remained vacant in AC II tier on Monday = (250 – 240) = 10

The number of seat remained vacant in AC II tier on Tuesday = (250 – 230) = 20

The number of seat remained vacant in AC II tier on Friday = (250 – 210) = 40

The number of seat remained vacant in AC 1st class on Monday = (150 – 145) = 5

The number of seat remained vacant in AC 1st class on Tuesday = (150 – 120) = 30

The number of seat remained vacant in AC 1st class on Friday = (150 – 130) = 20

Total number of vacant seat in all the AC classes on Monday, Tuesday and Friday = (20 + 50 + 10 + 20 + 40 + 5 + 30 + 20)

⇒ 195

The ratio of number of seats that remained vacant in all the Non-AC classes on Wednesday and Thursday taken together to number of seats remained vacant in AC classes on Monday, Tuesday and Friday = (310 : 195)

⇒ 62 : 39

**∴ The required ratio is 62 : 39**

The percentage of the population below the poverty level in the district D₃ is 20%

Number of people below the poverty line,

In how many schools, the number of girls is more than the average number of boys per school?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Number of schools = 5

FORMULAE USED:

average = sum of observations / number of observations

CALCULATION:

Number of Boys in School A = (9/17) × 680 = 360

Number of Boys in School B = (4/9) × 720 = 320

Number of Boys in School C = (5/18) × 540 = 150

Number of Boys in School D = (2/3) × 660 = 440

Number of Boys in School E = (13/25) × 900 = 468

Total number of Boys = 360 + 320 + 150 + 440 + 468 = 1738 

 

Average number of Boys per school = 1738/5 = 347.6

 

Number of Girls in School A = 680 - 360 = 320

Number of Girls in School B = 720 - 320 = 400

Number of Girls in School C = 540 - 150 = 390

Number of Girls in School D = 660 - 440 = 220

Number of Girls in School E = 900 - 468 = 432

 

∴ In 3 schools the number of girls is more than the average number of boys per school.
